svg.title: RIEMANN R5 — Theta lifts, periods and the Siegel-Weil formula: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 5 in one poster: its 61 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-theta-inputs, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: A member of a family in chap-families is a chain of definite unitary groups joined by theta lifts. To show that the families satisfy their conditions we need several facts about these lifts: that they do not vanish, that they separate vectors, that suitable test vectors have algebraic values, how their norms depend on L-values, and how the periods built from them behave. This chapter proves these facts. thm-theta-inputs collects them. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: A member of a family in chap-families is a chain of definite unitary groups joined by theta lifts. To show that the families satisfy their conditions we need several facts about these lifts: that they do not vanish, that they separate vectors, that suitable test vectors have algebraic values, how their norms depend on L-values, and
how the periods built from them behave. This chapter proves these facts. thm-theta-inputs collects them. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.
A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)
Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines (four on a short card). The footer gives its file and
line in the mirror and the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges. A proof use outside the chapter is counted, not drawn. Rows: a card's row is one above the highest card whose proof uses it, or higher
where that makes room; a card sits under the cards that use it where it can. A short card shows four lines of the signature and one paragraph of the proof.

text.tspan: Each step of the grid preserves cusp forms

svg.text: Suppose that twisted theta lifts along the grid, with the chosen test functions, send cusp forms
to cusp forms. Then for all large scales and every choice of test data, every arrow A → B of the
grid, every idempotent sum at the local places, every local vector f attached to the arrow and
every polynomial Q in the Fock model, the following holds: for each listed cusp form F on U(A)
the theta integral of F against the Fock vector of (f, Q) converges, and the lift is a listed cusp
By lem-theta-lift-smooth-cusp-forms the lifts are cuspidal for all smooth test functions.
Arrows of the grid go either to the right or down a flip. For the arrows to the right this is a cusp
transition; for the descending arrows one runs through the flips of the tower. …

text.tspan: 3 · The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….
The Siegel–Weil formula identifies the average of a theta function over an adelic unitary group
with a value of a Siegel Eisenstein series. We use it in several ranges. In Weil's range, where
both sides converge, it is Weil's theorem thm-siegel-weil-weil-range; its classical form,
Siegel's mass formula for hermitian forms thm-siegel-main-theorem-hermitian, gives the
mass constants of the later sections. Outside Weil's range we use the formula of Kudla–Rallis
and Ichino for Fock vectors thm-siegel-weil-outside-weil-range and its doubling form
thm-siegel-weil-convergent-doubling. The forms for definite spaces,
thm-siegel-weil-definite and thm-siegel-weil-definite-k, serve the theta towers
and the construction of Galois representations in chap-galois.

text.tspan: 2. Theta towers and their step identities

svg.text: A theta tower is a sequence of unitary dual pairs U(V) × U(W) in which the dimension of W
grows by two at each step. Its step identities (def-theta-tower-step,
thm-theta-tower-step-identities) say that matched theta integrals along the tower are
proportional, and that each step multiplies the constant by one partial Hecke L-value, as in the
Rallis inner product formula. The proof computes the constant terms of theta integrals along
the parabolic that fixes an isotropic plane and compares them, through the definite
Siegel–Weil formula, with those of Siegel Eisenstein series. Every later section uses these

text.tspan: 3. Non-vanishing and separation of theta lifts

svg.text: Two non-vanishing results for the theta lifts of a family. Theta functionals separate vectors (
thm-theta-functionals-separate): Howe duality at unramified places, the Siegel–Weil
formula and a quantitative branching law for discrete series give separation by real
functionals, and the ascent of Bessel periods up the tower (thm-bessel-period-ascent)
turns this into separation by Bessel periods. Downward theta lifts are nonzero and injective on
Hecke eigenspaces (thm-downward-theta-lift-nonvanishing): by the doubling method a
pole of the partial L-function gives a residue of a Siegel Eisenstein series, and this residue is a
theta integral from a smaller space (thm-siegel-eisenstein-residue-theta).
The slope bound of sec-theta-witt needs theta lifts with algebraic values.
thm-rational-test-vectors-theta shows that test vectors for the twisted theta lifts take
values in the field of the family, up to one constant and roots of unity. The proof checks that
each step of the grid of lifts sends cusp forms to cusp forms (
lem-grid-steps-preserve-cusp-forms), unfolds the twisted theta integral into a finite sum
of periods over a definite unitary group (lem-twisted-theta-unfolding), and compares the
twisted vacuum vectors with the base ones at real points.

text.tspan: 5. L-values along Witt towers and the indefinite slope bound

svg.text: This section proves the slope bound on the indefinite side (thm-indefinite-slope-bound):
the largest slope of the hermitian lattice there is at most its height minus the mean of logκ
over the twists. Iterating the step identities along a Witt tower expresses the ratios of square
constants of theta lifts through ratios of Hecke L-values (thm-witt-tower-square-ratios).
The non-vanishing of these values, bounds on their denominators and the functional equation
then bound the square ratios place by place (thm-square-term-estimates). The arithmetic
of the L-values comes from the results gathered in thm-non-endoscopic-hypotheses-hold.
The multiplicity condition, one of the basic conditions of
P_(u,t) of a family give, up to an isometry and nonzero constants, inner products of theta
lifts with projections. prop-isometric-period-identity proves this at every admissible
datum in three steps: a diagonal estimate from the Siegel–Weil formula and the archimedean
bounds of sec-theta-bessel; conditions at the points from the theory of discrete series; and
the identity for a real package (prop-period-identity-real-package), built from family
characters with links. The proof also uses a bound for sums over pairs of lattice terms, from
The archimedean estimates behind the period identity and the off-diagonal bound take place
on the real unitary group of signature (k+r, r+1), with the Bessel models of Gan, Gross and
Prasad for a subgroup U(k) (def-archimedean-bessel-data). The main theorem (
thm-bessel-transform-radial-space) says that Bessel transforms of compactly
supported functions satisfy the radial equations of invariant differential operators. With
Capelli's identity for the quantum determinant this gives pointwise (
thm-weighted-bessel-sum-bound) bounds for Bessel transforms of discrete series
coefficients, and archimedean models in which local integrals become energy forms (
Distinct types of a datum are almost orthogonal: thm-offdiagonal-bound gives
|K_0(u,u')|^2 ≤ (1 + b^(-6)) d_u d_(u')/D^* for u ≠ u'. The proof is an abstract
bound for a pairing over a CM field with nineteen inputs, which
prop-offdiagonal-hypotheses-hold checks for the families. The main inputs are
archimedean model data (prop-archimedean-model-data) and a decomposition of the pair
coefficients into local counts of partners and lattices (

text.tspan: 9. Counting automorphic forms and mass constants

svg.text: The family conditions need the number of automorphic forms of each type, with its main term
in terms of Siegel's mass constant. thm-counting-automorphic-forms-unitary counts
automorphic forms of a given type on unitary groups of large rank by a kernel argument, given
the volume step: splitting off an anisotropic line changes the Haar volume by the Siegel mass

laws for the kernels of the lattice chain (lem-five-laws-chain-kernels), whose two
bounds are integral moments of jets of theta kernels (lem-integral-moments-kernel-jets
